dse_runs.notes: System spec: p99 latency constraint is only an analytic bound at L1, so keep designs with latency margin for L2. Objective is min luts_plus_ffs with accuracy_bits >= 10 (max_abs_err <= 2^-10). Prefer area-lean families (iterative / small unroll) that still meet throughput_msps >= 2.

selected_facts.dds_provenance: simulated (hw_dse.l2.dds l2-v1: golden-model DDS, 32-bit phase accumulator, coherent 16384-point FFT, tone bin 1297)

l2.why: the L1 selection passes the simulated system constraints

l3: not verified in this campaign: no recorded L3 row; a fresh exhaustive run (W=14) is too heavy for a live campaign

final_text: The single spec in the queue, `bursty_offload`, is finalized. I spent its full 400-eval L1 budget in one structured `run_dse` pass (inner graph: map_front → refine → map_front → stop), which produced a 39-design feasible, non-dominated front; the area-lean `pipelined_m` family dominated. L2 `simulate_system` on the top 6 confirmed the L1 winner under the bursty Poisson system scenario — the analytic p99 bounds were optimistic (e.g. 0.0964 → 0.1066 us) but every shortlisted design still passed the 0.4 us limit, and the winner was unchanged. L3/L4/L5 produced no new numbers: `verify_rtl` had no recorded L3 row for this configuration (a fresh W=14 exhaustive run is too heavy live), `synthesize` had no recorded L4 result, and `back_annotate` returned `no_measured_data` with no WINNER CHANGE flagged, so no `reexplore` was warranted. The finalized selection by the spec's rule (min luts_plus_ffs) is `pipelined_m:data_width=14,n_iter=12,angle_guard=2,frac_guard=2,rounding=trunc,m=3` — luts_plus_ffs=877 (631 LUTs + 246 FFs, estimate), accuracy_bits=10.1 with max_abs_err=0.000894 (2^-10.13, exact), throughput_msps=124 (estimate), and sys_p99_latency_us=0.107 (simulated), satisfying all three constraints (throughput ≥ 2, err ≤ 2^-10, p99 ≤ 0.4 us).
